resources.string: This build has internet permission only for the backup to a server you run yourself, which is off until you set it up. Nothing else uses the network.

Copies your photos and videos to a server you run yourself, over an encrypted connection. Nothing leaves this phone until you turn the backup on, it goes only to the server below, and eikon never deletes or changes anything on it. The password or key is kept encrypted, in the Android Keystore.
Saved. Leave empty to keep it
In Immich: Account settings, API keys, New API key. The permission it needs is asset.upload.
In Nextcloud: Personal settings, Security, Devices and sessions, create a new app password. Use that, not your login password.
The certificate was not trusted, so nothing was sent and nothing will be.
This server\'s certificate is not from an authority your phone trusts

%1$s presented the certificate below. Compare its fingerprint with the one your server shows (for example with: openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256). Trust it only if they are identical: from then on this one certificate is accepted for this server, and no other.
It is signed by itself, as the certificate of a home server usually is.
Back up my photos and videos
Save and test the connection first.
Hidden photos will be sent to your server too, where they are as visible as anything else there.

resources.string: Android hides where photos were taken from apps that do not have the photo-location permission, so the copies on your server would have no location.
